guidance: {"kind": "procedure_guidance_v2", "procedure": "Audit the next action using only supplied public evidence and the execution catalog. First extract the latest request target and operation in its own terms. Separate the target entity from contextual words such as job or work. Then recover any still-active originating request, continuation trigger, ordering revision and cancellation. A continuation can activate an earlier authorization without issuing a new request. Match the target entity and requested operation against the candidate catalog scope AND its prerequisites. Reject a candidate when its scope excludes the requested entity even if contextual words sound similar. Do not infer the task category merely from the word job. Correlate receipts with the exact submitted action and target; partial success does not discharge the remaining obligation. Before recommending termination, check every authorized pending or suspended obligation and its trigger, including conditional final work. Do not interpret missing recent mention as cancellation. Return only the unchanged schema fields recommendation, basis_ids, uncertainty. In recommendation use compact Target, Authority, Match, Action labels. Treat a continuation as activating the latest still-live authorized obligation only when the ledger preserves its trigger, scope, order position and incomplete extent. Correlate receipts to the exact submitted skill, target and extent; distinguish submitted, partial, native-complete and canceled. Select the next catalog action whose scope and prerequisites match that live obligation, including revised ordering; do not let a generic word or stale summary override explicit evidence. If no unique match is supported, abstain. Cite up to five existing public evidence IDs; uncertainty states only an evidenced conflict or unmet prerequisite. The actor decides. Treat memory as fallible: prefer explicit public requests and correlated receipts over summary assertions. Never execute, veto, invent evidence, or use private evaluator information. The actor decides."}
update: {"kind": "procedure_update_v2", "procedure": "Consolidate public requests and correlated execution receipts into a compact obligation ledger in the existing memory text. Preserve for each live obligation: origin event, target, requested operation, activation or continuation condition, current ordering and revision event, status, and latest correlated receipt. Record conditional future work as authorized but waiting for its stated condition, not unauthorized. Distinguish authorization from readiness and completion. Carry forward the originating authorization and continuation trigger across unrelated intervening work. A short continuation request need not repeat the original authorization. Remove an obligation only on an explicit applicable cancellation or a receipt proving its requested extent complete. One successful segment leaves the remainder pending when the request requires more. A submitted action is only a commitment until the correlated receipt. A revision changes only its stated scope; retain the original ordering needed to resolve relative references. Before saving, check each previously pending or conditional obligation: either retain it with its trigger, or cite the cancellation/completion event that discharges it. Never turn an actor assumption about authorization into a user restriction. Preserve unresolved conflicts as uncertain. Within the shared memory budget prioritize live obligations and evidence IDs over coordinates or verbose completed-job descriptions; compact discharged jobs. Do not invent a plan, task, restriction, dependency or completion. History records the actual change and its evidence."}
